The stepper drives a screw that pushes up the pins. The pusher part is just an insert that slides down inside. 
Given the timeframe, I have to choose what is most likely to work, even though you can see it still took a number of revisions (I don't even think that was all)
In the end, the number of pins had to be reduced (kept getting 'bed of nails' effect) and the vacuum needed to be embedded in the tip with some internal chambers as I was having a hard time getting seals any other way. 
As I've understood the design requirements more, I think I would try for some voice coil/solenoid options for the pins and that would allow for smaller space and fidelity on the for pin selection? That's the idea, but need to move to other areas now.

Author: anfroholic
Content:
I will have a bunch to share in the coming days, for now I'll just share a snippet of code that basically runs the whole show. 

I thought this bit was kinda beautiful. 
```py
def sort(self, todo):
    """Do the sort
    Machine consists of 3 major components. pusher, tobor, feeders
    Certain components can be working on the next die while waiting on others 
    run_together() allows for this by blocking until both are completed
    """
    for placed, die, upcoming in pipeline(todo, size=3):
        yield from self.run_together(
            self.pick(die),                   # tobor: down onto die N, pins up, lift
            self.feeder_ready(placed, die))   # feeder: past N-1's pocket, right tape, pocket found
        yield from self.run_together(
            self.carry(die),                  # tobor: up camera, align, into the pocket
            self.pusher_under(upcoming))      # pusher: already off under die N+1
        yield from self.checkpoint(die)
```
